107: static int sdio_wait_command(struct bk7258_sdio_s *priv, uint32_t cmd)
108: {
109:   clock_t deadline = clock_systime_ticks() + MSEC2TICK(1000);
110:   uint32_t status;
111: 
112:   for (;;)
113:     {
114:       status = sdio_read(BK7258_SDIO_INT_STATUS);
115:       if ((status & (BK7258_SDIO_CMD_NO_RESPONSE |
116:                      BK7258_SDIO_CMD_RESPONSE_END |
117:                      BK7258_SDIO_CMD_TIMEOUT)) != 0)
118:         {
119:           break;
120:         }
121: 
122:       if ((int32_t)(clock_systime_ticks() - deadline) >= 0)
123:         {
124:           printf("SDIO CMD%u timeout status=0x%08lx\n",
125:                  (unsigned)(cmd & MMCSD_CMDIDX_MASK),
126:                  (unsigned long)status);
127:           return -ETIMEDOUT;
128:         }
129: 
130:       /* At transfer speed the RX FIFO can fill before a 100 us sleep
131:        * expires.  Keep the PIO loop tight while data is active; otherwise a
132:        * 512-byte sector consistently overflows after the first 256 bytes. */
133:       if (!priv->data_active)
134:         {
135:           nxsig_usleep(100);
136:         }
137:     }
138: 
139:   sdio_write(BK7258_SDIO_INT_STATUS,
140:              status & (BK7258_SDIO_CMD_NO_RESPONSE |
141:                        BK7258_SDIO_CMD_RESPONSE_END |
142:                        BK7258_SDIO_CMD_TIMEOUT |
143:                        BK7258_SDIO_CMD_CRC_OK |
144:                        BK7258_SDIO_CMD_CRC_FAIL));
145: 
146:   if ((status & BK7258_SDIO_CMD_TIMEOUT) != 0)
147:     {
148:       printf("SDIO CMD%u response timeout status=0x%08lx\n",
149:              (unsigned)(cmd & MMCSD_CMDIDX_MASK),
150:              (unsigned long)status);
151:       return -ETIMEDOUT;
152:     }
153: 
154:   /* The BK7258 host reports CRC failure for the open-drain/long-response
155:    * identification commands even when the vendor stack accepts the response.
156:    * Armino explicitly tolerates this for ACMD41, CMD2 and CMD9.  Keep the
157:    * same compatibility rule while preserving CRC errors for normal R1/R7.
158:    */
159:   if ((status & BK7258_SDIO_CMD_CRC_FAIL) != 0 &&

162:       (cmd & MMCSD_CMDIDX_MASK) != MMCSD_CMDIDX9)
163:     {

168:     }

170:   return OK;

191:       (cmd & MMCSD_CMDIDX_MASK) != MMCSD_CMDIDX9 &&
192:       (cmd & MMCSD_CMDIDX_MASK) != SD_ACMDIDX41)

321: static int sdio_recvsetup(FAR struct sdio_dev_s *dev, FAR uint8_t *buffer,
322:                           size_t nbytes)
323: {
324:   FAR struct bk7258_sdio_s *priv = (FAR struct bk7258_sdio_s *)dev;
325:   uint32_t value;
326: 
327:   if (buffer == NULL || nbytes == 0 || priv->blocklen == 0 ||
328:       nbytes > (priv->blocklen * priv->nblocks))
329:     {
330:       return -EINVAL;
331:     }
332: 
333:   value = sdio_read(BK7258_SDIO_FIFO);
334:   value &= ~(0xffffu | BK7258_SDIO_FIFO_RX_RESET |
335:              BK7258_SDIO_STATE_RESET | BK7258_SDIO_CLOCK_GATE);
336:   value |= 0x0101u | BK7258_SDIO_FIFO_RX_RESET |
337:            BK7258_SDIO_STATE_RESET | BK7258_SDIO_SAMPLE_POSITIVE;
338:   sdio_write(BK7258_SDIO_FIFO, value);
339: 
340:   sdio_write(BK7258_SDIO_INT_STATUS,
341:              BK7258_SDIO_DATA_RECEIVE_END |
342:              BK7258_SDIO_DATA_TIMEOUT |
343:              BK7258_SDIO_RX_NEED_READ |
344:              BK7258_SDIO_FIFO_OVERFLOW |
345:              BK7258_SDIO_DATA_CRC_OK |
346:              BK7258_SDIO_DATA_CRC_FAIL);
347: 
348:   /* BK7258 V2 uses this receive-engine mode for block reads.  CMD17 still
349:    * bounds the card-side transfer to one sector. */
350:   value = ((priv->blocklen << BK7258_SDIO_DATA_BLOCK_SHIFT) &
351:            BK7258_SDIO_DATA_BLOCK_MASK) | BK7258_SDIO_DATA_BYTE_SELECT |
352:            BK7258_SDIO_DATA_MULTIBLOCK;
353:   sdio_write(BK7258_SDIO_DATA_CTRL, value | BK7258_SDIO_DATA_ENABLE);
354:   modifyreg32(BK7258_SDCARD_DATA_CTRL_ALIAS,
355:               BK7258_SDIO_DATA_BLOCK_MASK,
356:               (priv->blocklen << BK7258_SDIO_DATA_BLOCK_SHIFT) &
357:               BK7258_SDIO_DATA_BLOCK_MASK);
358:   sdio_write(BK7258_SDIO_DATA_TIMER, BK7258_SDIO_TIMEOUT);
359:   priv->buffer = buffer;
360:   priv->remaining = nbytes;
361:   priv->data_active = true;
362:   printf("SDIO data setup block=%lu count=%lu bytes=%lu\n",
363:          (unsigned long)priv->blocklen, (unsigned long)priv->nblocks,
364:          (unsigned long)nbytes);
365:   return OK;
366: }

400: static void sdio_drain_fifo(FAR struct bk7258_sdio_s *priv)
401: {
402:   unsigned int count = 32;
403: 
404:   while (priv->remaining != 0 && count-- != 0 &&
405:          (sdio_read(BK7258_SDIO_FIFO) & BK7258_SDIO_RX_READY) != 0)
406:     {
407:       uint32_t word = sdio_read(BK7258_SDIO_RX_FIFO);
408:       size_t copy = priv->remaining < sizeof(word) ? priv->remaining :
409:                     sizeof(word);
410: 
411:       memcpy(priv->buffer, &word, copy);
412:       priv->buffer += copy;
413:       priv->remaining -= copy;
414:     }

417: int bk7258_sdio_read_blocks(FAR uint8_t *buffer, uint32_t sector,
418:                             unsigned int nblocks)
419: {
420:   FAR struct sdio_dev_s *dev;
421:   FAR struct bk7258_sdio_s *priv;
422:   sdio_eventset_t event;
423:   unsigned int i;
424:   unsigned int nonff = 0;
425:   uint32_t hash = 2166136261u;
426:   uint32_t response;
427:   uint32_t value;
428:   int ret;
429: 
430:   if (buffer == NULL || nblocks == 0 || nblocks > 1)
431:     {
432:       return -EINVAL;
433:     }
434: 
435:   dev = bk7258_sdio_initialize(0);
436:   if (dev == NULL)
437:     {
438:       return -ENODEV;
439:     }
440: 
441:   priv = (FAR struct bk7258_sdio_s *)dev;
442:   ret = nxmutex_lock(&priv->io_lock);
443:   if (ret < 0)
444:     {
445:       return ret;
446:     }
447: 
448:   SDIO_BLOCKSETUP(dev, 512, 1);
449:   SDIO_WAITENABLE(dev, SDIOWAIT_TRANSFERDONE | SDIOWAIT_TIMEOUT |
450:                   SDIOWAIT_ERROR, 2000);
451:   ret = SDIO_RECVSETUP(dev, buffer, 512);
452:   if (ret == OK)
453:     {
454:       /* The BK7258 V2 vendor path uses CMD18 for block reads, including a
455:        * one-block request. OCR=0x80ff8000 has CCS clear, so the address is in
456:        * bytes rather than 512-byte blocks. */
457:       ret = SDIO_SENDCMD(dev, MMCSD_CMD18, sector << 9);
458:     }
459:   if (ret == OK)
460:     {
461:       ret = SDIO_WAITRESPONSE(dev, MMCSD_CMD18);
462:     }
463:   if (ret == OK)
464:     {
465:        ret = SDIO_RECVR1(dev, MMCSD_CMD18, &response);
466:     }
467:   if (ret == OK)
468:     {
469:       event = SDIO_EVENTWAIT(dev);
470:       if ((event & SDIOWAIT_TRANSFERDONE) == 0)
471:         {
472:           ret = (event & SDIOWAIT_TIMEOUT) != 0 ? -ETIMEDOUT : -EIO;
473:         }
474:     }
475: 
476:   if (ret == OK)
477:     {
478:       /* Stop the card-side read state after the requested block. */
479:       sdio_write(BK7258_SDIO_DATA_CTRL, 0);
480:       value = sdio_read(BK7258_SDIO_FIFO);
481:       value &= ~(BK7258_SDIO_FIFO_RX_RESET | BK7258_SDIO_STATE_RESET);
482:       value |= BK7258_SDIO_CLOCK_GATE;
483:       sdio_write(BK7258_SDIO_FIFO, value);
484: 
485:       ret = SDIO_SENDCMD(dev, MMCSD_CMD12, 0);
486:       if (ret == OK)
487:         {
488:           ret = SDIO_WAITRESPONSE(dev, MMCSD_CMD12);
489:         }
490:       if (ret == OK)
491:         {
492:           ret = SDIO_RECVR1(dev, MMCSD_CMD12, &response);
493:         }
494: 
495:       modifyreg32(BK7258_SDIO_FIFO, BK7258_SDIO_CLOCK_GATE, 0);
496:       value = sdio_read(BK7258_SDIO_FIFO);
497:       value &= ~(BK7258_SDIO_FIFO_RX_RESET | BK7258_SDIO_STATE_RESET);
498:       sdio_write(BK7258_SDIO_FIFO, value);
499:     }
500: 
501:   for (i = 0; i < nblocks; i++)
502:     {
503:       (void)i;
504:     }
505: 
506:   if (ret == OK)
507:     {
508:       int signature = -1;
509: 
510:       for (i = 0; i < 512; i++)
511:         {
512:           hash = (hash ^ buffer[i]) * 16777619u;
513:           if (buffer[i] != 0xff)
514:             {
515:               nonff++;
516:             }
517: 
518:           if (i != 0 && buffer[i - 1] == 0x55 && buffer[i] == 0xaa)
519:             {
520:               signature = (int)i - 1;
521:             }
522:         }
523: 
524:       printf("SDIO sector=%lu nonff=%u hash=%08lx first=%02x%02x%02x%02x "
525:              "last=%02x%02x%02x%02x signature=%d\n",
526:              (unsigned long)sector, nonff, (unsigned long)hash,
527:              buffer[0], buffer[1], buffer[2], buffer[3],
528:              buffer[508], buffer[509], buffer[510], buffer[511], signature);
529:     }
530: 
531:   nxmutex_unlock(&priv->io_lock);
532:   return ret;
533: }

535: static sdio_eventset_t sdio_eventwait(FAR struct sdio_dev_s *dev)
536: {
537:   FAR struct bk7258_sdio_s *priv = (FAR struct bk7258_sdio_s *)dev;
538:   clock_t deadline = priv->wait_start + MSEC2TICK(priv->wait_timeout);
539: 
540:   for (;;)
541:     {
542:       uint32_t status = sdio_read(BK7258_SDIO_INT_STATUS);
543: 
544:       if (priv->data_active)
545:         {
546:           sdio_drain_fifo(priv);
547:         }
548: 
549:       if ((status & (BK7258_SDIO_DATA_TIMEOUT |
550:                       BK7258_SDIO_DATA_CRC_FAIL |
551:                       BK7258_SDIO_FIFO_OVERFLOW)) != 0)
552:         {
553:           clock_t drain_deadline = clock_systime_ticks() + MSEC2TICK(10);
554: 
555:           while (priv->remaining != 0 &&
556:                  (int32_t)(clock_systime_ticks() - drain_deadline) < 0)
557:             {
558:               sdio_drain_fifo(priv);
559:             }
560: 
561:           printf("SDIO data error status=0x%08lx remaining=%lu\n",
562:                  (unsigned long)status, (unsigned long)priv->remaining);
563:           sdio_write(BK7258_SDIO_INT_STATUS,
564:                       status & (BK7258_SDIO_DATA_RECEIVE_END |
565:                                 BK7258_SDIO_DATA_TIMEOUT |
566:                                 BK7258_SDIO_RX_NEED_READ |
567:                                 BK7258_SDIO_DATA_CRC_FAIL |
568:                                 BK7258_SDIO_FIFO_OVERFLOW |
569:                                 BK7258_SDIO_DATA_CRC_OK));
570:           priv->data_active = false;
571:           if ((status & (BK7258_SDIO_DATA_TIMEOUT |
572:                          BK7258_SDIO_FIFO_OVERFLOW)) == 0 &&
573:               priv->remaining == 0)
574:             {
575:               /* The board's SD-NAND asserts the BK7258 data CRC-fail status
576:                * after 512-byte reads even though the complete payload is in
577:                * the FIFO.  Accept only complete transfers; the read-only
578:                * fallback additionally validates the boot sector and FAT. */
579:               priv->wake_events = SDIOWAIT_TRANSFERDONE;
580:               printf("SDIO complete payload accepted despite CRC status\n");
581:             }
582:           else
583:             {
584:               priv->wake_events = SDIOWAIT_ERROR;
585:             }
586:           break;
587:         }
588: 
589:       if (priv->data_active &&
590:           (status & BK7258_SDIO_DATA_RECEIVE_END) != 0)
591:         {
592:           sdio_drain_fifo(priv);
593:           sdio_write(BK7258_SDIO_INT_STATUS,
594:                      status & (BK7258_SDIO_DATA_RECEIVE_END |
595:                                BK7258_SDIO_DATA_CRC_OK |
596:                                BK7258_SDIO_RX_NEED_READ));
597:           priv->data_active = false;
598:           priv->wake_events = priv->remaining == 0 ?
599:                               SDIOWAIT_TRANSFERDONE : SDIOWAIT_ERROR;
600:           printf("SDIO data complete status=0x%08lx remaining=%lu event=0x%x\n",
601:                  (unsigned long)status, (unsigned long)priv->remaining,
602:                  priv->wake_events);
603:           break;
604:         }
605: 
606:       if ((int32_t)(clock_systime_ticks() - deadline) >= 0)
607:         {
608:           priv->data_active = false;
609:           priv->wake_events = SDIOWAIT_TIMEOUT;
610:           printf("SDIO data timeout status=0x%08lx remaining=%lu\n",
611:                  (unsigned long)status, (unsigned long)priv->remaining);
612:           break;
613:         }
614: 
615:       if (!priv->data_active)
616:         {
617:           nxsig_usleep(100);
618:         }
619:     }
620: 
621:   priv->wait_events = 0;
622:   return priv->wake_events;
623: }

763: bk_err_t bk_sdio_host_wait_cmd_response(uint32_t cmd_index)
764: {
765: #if CONFIG_SDIO_V2P0
766: 	bk_err_t ret = BK_OK;
767: 	uint32_t msg = 0;
768: #endif
769: 
770: 	SDIO_HOST_RETURN_ON_NOT_INIT();
771: 	SDIO_PM_CHECK_RESTORE(0);
772: 
773: 	uint32_t int_status = sdio_host_hal_get_interrupt_status(&s_sdio_host.hal);
774: 
775: #if CONFIG_SDIO_V2P0
776: 	{
777: 		//TODO:Timeout and CRC fail should use different case
778: 		//FreeRTOS doesn't use EVENT,so use msg queue.
779: 		ret = rtos_pop_from_queue(&s_sdio_host.irq_cmd_msg, &msg, SDIO_CMD_WAIT_TIME);
780: 		if(ret)
781: 		{
782: 			SDIO_HOST_LOGV("sdio wait slave CMD%d timeout, int_status=0x%x, ret=%d\r\n", cmd_index, int_status, ret);
783: 			return BK_ERR_SDIO_HOST_CMD_RSP_TIMEOUT;
784: 		}
785: 	}
786: #else
787: 	/* wait until cmd response */
788: 	BK_WHILE (!sdio_host_hal_is_cmd_rsp_interrupt_triggered(&s_sdio_host.hal, int_status)) {
789: 		int_status = sdio_host_hal_get_interrupt_status(&s_sdio_host.hal);
790: 	}
791: 
792: 	/* clear command response int status */
793: 	sdio_host_hal_clear_cmd_rsp_interrupt_status(&s_sdio_host.hal, int_status);
794: 
795: 	if (sdio_host_hal_is_cmd_rsp_timeout_interrupt_triggered(&s_sdio_host.hal, int_status)) {
796: 		if (cmd_index != SEND_OP_COND) {
797: 			SDIO_HOST_LOGW("sdio wait slave CMD%d timeout\r\n", cmd_index);
798: 			return BK_ERR_SDIO_HOST_CMD_RSP_TIMEOUT;
799: 		}
800: 	}
801: 
802: 	if (sdio_host_hal_is_cmd_rsp_crc_fail_interrupt_triggered(&s_sdio_host.hal, int_status)) {
803: 		if ((cmd_index != SD_APP_OP_COND) &&
804: 			(cmd_index != ALL_SEND_CID) &&
805: 			(cmd_index != SEND_CSD) &&
806: 			(cmd_index != SEND_OP_COND)) {
807: 			SDIO_HOST_LOGW("sdio receive slave CMD%d crc fail\r\n", cmd_index);
808: 			return BK_ERR_SDIO_HOST_CMD_RSP_CRC_FAIL;
809: 		}
810: 	}
811: #endif
812: 	return BK_OK;
813: }

946: static bk_err_t sdio_host_cpu_write_fifo(const uint8_t *write_data, uint32_t data_size)
947: {
948: 	BK_RETURN_ON_NULL(write_data);
949: 	SDIO_HOST_RETURN_ON_NOT_INIT();
950: 	SDIO_PM_CHECK_RESTORE(0);
951: 
952: 	sdio_host_hal_t *hal = &s_sdio_host.hal;
953: 	uint32_t index = 0;
954: #if (CONFIG_SDIO_DEBUG_SUPPORT || CONFIG_SOC_BK7256XX)
955: 	uint32 data_tmp = 0;
956: #endif
957: 	bk_err_t error_state = BK_OK;
958: 	uint32_t i = 0;
959: 
960: 	while ((index < data_size)) {
961: 		//confirm can write data to fifo(fifo isn't at busy/full status)
962: 		while((sdio_host_hal_is_tx_fifo_write_ready(hal)) == 0)
963: 		{
964: 			i++;
965: 
966: 			if(i % 0x400000 == 0) {
967: 				SDIO_HOST_LOGW("FIFO can't write i=0x%08x.\r\n", i);
968: 				SDIO_HOST_LOGW("=== RESET SDCARD ===\r\n");
969: 				error_state = BK_ERR_SDIO_HOST_DATA_TIMEOUT;
970: 				return error_state;
971: 			}
972: 
973: 		}
974: 
975: //NOTES:SDIO V1P0:write data should be reverted sequence by software, and read data should revert by ASIC of "SD_BYTE_SEL"
976: //or the endian isn't match with windows system.
977: //From BK7258XX, the write data sequence is reverted by ASIC hardware,without any config of "SD_BYTE_SEL"
978: #if CONFIG_SOC_BK7256XX	//after BK7258 V5 chip, ASIC chip TX no needs software revert data.
979: 		//switch byte sequence, as the SDIO transfer data with big-endian
980: 		data_tmp = ((write_data[index] << 24) | (write_data[index + 1] << 16) | (write_data[index + 2] << 8) | write_data[index + 3]);
981: 		sdio_host_hal_write_fifo(hal, data_tmp);
982: #else
983: #if (CONFIG_SDIO_DEBUG_SUPPORT)
984: 		data_tmp = *(uint32_t *)&write_data[index];
985: #endif
986: 		sdio_host_hal_write_fifo(hal, *(uint32_t *)&write_data[index]);
987: #endif
988: 
989: 		index += 4;
990: 
991: #if (CONFIG_SDIO_DEBUG_SUPPORT)
992: 		if(index < 16)
993: 		{
994: 			SDIO_HOST_LOGV("data_tmp=0x%08x", data_tmp);
995: 		}
996: 		if(index == 16)
997: 		{
998: 			SDIO_HOST_LOGV("0x%08x\r\n", data_tmp);
999: 		}
1000: #endif
1001: 		//first block finish, enable tx fifo clock gate and then start write data to sdio wires(sdcard)
1002: 		if((index == SDIO_BLOCK_SIZE))
1003: 		{
1004: 			bk_sdio_tx_fifo_clk_gate_config(1);
1005: 			sdio_host_hal_start_send_data(&s_sdio_host.hal);
1006: 		}
1007: 
1008: 		//one block write to sdcard fifo finish
1009: 		if((index % SDIO_BLOCK_SIZE == 0) || (index == data_size))	//maybe isn't a full block(though sdcard always use full block)
1010: 		{
1011: 			/*
1012: 			 * wait write end int which means the data has sent to sdcard and get the sdcard's response.
1013: 			 * empty mask just mean host FIFO is empty but can't indicate that sdcard has dealed data finish.
1014: 			 * write status fail will not set semaphore yet, so it cause here timeout, here set it as tx fail.
1015: 			 */
1016: 			s_sdio_host.is_tx_blocked = true;
1017: 			error_state = rtos_get_semaphore(&(s_sdio_host.tx_sema), SDIO_MAX_TX_WAIT_TIME);
1018: 			if(error_state)
1019: 			{
1020: 				s_sdio_host.is_tx_blocked = false;
1021: 				SDIO_HOST_LOGW("TODO:sdio tx data fail:index=%d!\r\n", index);
1022: 			}
1023: 		}
1024: 	}
1025: 
1026: 	return error_state;
1027: }

1029: bk_err_t bk_sdio_host_write_fifo(const uint8_t *write_data, uint32_t data_size)
1030: {
1031: #if CONFIG_SDIO_GDMA_EN
1032: 	if(s_sdio_host.dma_tx_en)
1033: 		return sdio_dma_write_fifo(write_data, data_size);
1034: 	else
1035: 		return sdio_host_cpu_write_fifo(write_data, data_size);

1037: 	return sdio_host_cpu_write_fifo(write_data, data_size);

1057: 	SDIO_PM_CHECK_RESTORE(0);

1061: 	error_state = rtos_get_semaphore(&(s_sdio_host.rx_sema), SDIO_MAX_RX_WAIT_TIME);
1062: 	if(error_state != BK_OK)

1068: 		error_state = BK_ERR_SDIO_HOST_DATA_CRC_FAIL;
1069: 		s_sdio_host_data_crc_error = false;
1070: 		SDIO_HOST_LOGD("func %s, line %d, return crc error.\r\n", __func__, __LINE__);
1071: 	}

1073:

1078: bk_err_t bk_sdio_host_write_fifo(const uint8_t *write_data, uint32_t data_size)
1079: {
1080: 	BK_RETURN_ON_NULL(write_data);
1081: 	SDIO_HOST_RETURN_ON_NOT_INIT();
1082: 	SDIO_PM_CHECK_RESTORE(0);
1083: 
1084: 	sdio_host_hal_t *hal = &s_sdio_host.hal;
1085: 	uint32_t index = 0;
1086: 	uint32 data_tmp = 0;
1087: 	uint32_t int_level = 0;
1088: 	bk_err_t error_state = BK_OK;
1089: 
1090: 	while ((sdio_host_hal_is_tx_fifo_write_ready(hal)) && (index < data_size)) {
1091: 		data_tmp = ((write_data[index] << 24) | (write_data[index + 1] << 16) | (write_data[index + 2] << 8) | write_data[index + 3]);

1200: {

1203: 	uint32_t data_size = blk_cnt * 512;

1205: 	//read data from SDIO to buffer
1206: 	while (bk_sdio_host_wait_receive_data() == BK_OK) {

1209: 			error_state = bk_sdio_host_read_fifo(&read_data);
1210: 			if(error_state == BK_OK)
1211: 			{
1212: 				data[index++] = read_data & 0xff;
1213: 				data[index++] = (read_data >> 8) & 0xff;
1214: 				data[index++] = (read_data >> 16) & 0xff;
1215: 				data[index++] = (read_data >> 24) & 0xff;
1216: 				//SDIO_HOST_LOGV("read_data:%x, index:%d\r\n", read_data, index);
1217: 			}
1218: 			else
1219: 			{
1220: 				SDIO_HOST_LOGW("Read FIFO fail,index=%d\r\n", index);
1221: 				break;
1222: 			}
1223: 		} while ((index % SDIO_BLOCK_SIZE) != 0);
1224: 
1225: 		if (index >= data_size) {
1226: 			SDIO_HOST_LOGV("rx data finish bytes:%d\r\n", index);
1227: 			break;
1228: 		}
1229: 
1230: //maybe some files in SDCARD and read it takes too much time, then cause WDT timeout
1231: #if (CONFIG_TASK_WDT)
1232: 		bk_task_wdt_feed();
1233: #endif
1234: 	}
1235: 
1236: 	//CRC fail or some of block timeout and so on
1237: 	if (index != data_size)
1238: 	{
1239: 		error_state = BK_ERR_SDIO_HOST_DATA_CRC_FAIL;
1240: 		SDIO_HOST_LOGW("func %s, read data fail,rx real cnt=%d,request cnt=%d, error_state=%d\r\n", __func__, index, data_size, error_state);
1241: 
1242: 	}
1243: 
1244: 	return error_state;
1245: }

**Conclusion**

The current BK7258 contest path has several independent divergences from the AP HAL/vendor implementation. The most important are:

1. It configures a one-sector transfer as multi-block: `DATA_MULTIBLOCK` plus `CMD18`.
2. It does not perform the vendor-required low-active FIFO/state reset sequence.
3. It enables automatic clock gating while reading, but stops the transfer and sends `CMD12` without first resetting the SDIO receive/state machine.
4. It uses a legacy hardcoded `0x448b000c` data-control alias in addition to the canonical BK7258 AP register.
5. It deliberately converts a data CRC failure into success.
6. It forces positive-edge sampling and does not explicitly establish the vendor default `CLK_REC_SEL=1`.
7. The PIO read loop is structurally compatible with the vendor FIFO access, but the data engine is misframed before the loop runs.

The observed `55 AA` at destination offset 170 is not explained by ordinary byte swapping. The MBR signature is normally at source offsets 510 and 511. `510 / 3 = 170`, so the symptom represents a three-to-one stream/index relationship, not a four-byte endian permutation. The simultaneous data CRC failure strongly indicates that the controller is receiving or framing more data than the software believes it is receiving, most plausibly because the read is configured as a multi-block `CMD18` transaction and the controller continues its pre-read behavior.

**8. CRC handling**

The contest explicitly accepts a CRC failure if all 512 requested bytes have been copied:

- [bk7258_sdio.c:549-580](/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/contest2026_264_VelaSightsuixingAIzhinengyanjing/board/beken/chips/bk7258/bk7258_sdio.c:549)

- [sdio_host_driver.c:1391-1421](/home/mi/vela_competition/bk_avdk_smp/ap/middleware/driver/sdio_host/sdio_host_driver.c:1391)
- [sdcard_driver.c:346-364](/home/mi/vela_competition/bk_avdk_smp/ap/middleware/driver/sdcard/sdio_driver.c:346)

Recommended behavior:

```text
if DATA_TIMEOUT or FIFO_OVERFLOW:
    fail

if DATA_CRC_FAIL:
    reset FIFO/state
    fail

if DATA_RECEIVE_END and remaining == 0:
    succeed
```

Do not convert `DATA_CRC_FAIL` into `SDIOWAIT_TRANSFERDONE`. A complete byte count does not prove that the bytes belong to the requested, CRC-valid block.

The actual bit masks used by the vendor low-level code are correct:

- `DATA_CRC_OK = BIT(12)`
- `DATA_CRC_FAIL = BIT(13)`

The contest header uses these two bits correctly at [bk7258_sdio.h:49-52](/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/contest2026_264_VelaSightsuixingAIzhinengyanjing/board/beken/chips/bk7258/hardware/bk7258_sdio.h:49).

Thus the working standard `CMD17` path is bypassed and every fallback read reaches the contest’s custom `CMD18` implementation. The minimal integration recommendation is to retain the standard MMCSD driver when probe succeeds; only install the fixed-geometry fallback after a failed probe, and ensure that the fallback performs the required card initialization/CMD16 itself.

**Recommended minimal change set**

The highest-confidence root cause is the combination of `DATA_MULTIBLOCK + CMD18` with the missing low-active FIFO/state reset. The next most important correction is to stop accepting the resulting CRC failure as success.
